name: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

date.note: Journal issue year; no month/day was captured from the fetched page.

title: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

claim.quote: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

summary.plain: The Homestake chlorine detector had been measuring solar neutrinos since 1970; this paper reports the combined result of 108 extractions, a solar-neutrino-induced argon-37 production rate of 2.56 SNU. In his Nobel lecture Raymond Davis Jr. sets the measured 2.56 SNU against the standard solar model's 7.6 SNU, about a third of the predicted rate: the solar neutrino problem.
summary.technical: Combined result of 108 extractions by the Homestake chlorine detector, which had been measuring the solar neutrino flux since 1970: solar-neutrino-induced 37Ar production rate of 2.56 ± 0.16 (stat) ± 0.16 (syst) SNU. Davis's Nobel lecture gives the standard solar model prediction of the time as 7.6 (+1.3/−1.1) SNU (Bahcall et al., 2001).

why_it_matters.value: The summary of all data from the multi-decade Homestake chlorine-detector experiment (Cleveland et al. 1998): a measured rate of 2.56 SNU against a standard solar model prediction of 7.6 SNU, about one-third of the predicted rate, the 'solar neutrino problem'.
why_it_matters.locator: Davis, Nobel Lecture, sections on the chlorine experiment results and the solar neutrino problem
why_it_matters.quote: the current value from the Homestake chlorine experiment is 2.56 SNU (Cleveland et al., 1998) and the current prediction of the standard solar model is 7.6 SNU (Bahcall et al., 2001). ... Cleveland et al. (1998) summarized all of the data from the Homestake experiment.
why_it_matters.note: Wording follows the Davis Nobel lecture (src:rf06-davis-nobel-lecture-2002). Corrected 2026-10-28: the earlier value repeated Davis's shorthand that "the Sun produces one-third as many neutrinos as expected", which reads as a claim about the Sun; the lecture compares the measured Homestake rate with the standard solar model's prediction (2.56 SNU against 7.6 SNU), so the Atlas states that comparison. The earlier phrasing about motivating SNO, Super-Kamiokande and GALLEX/SAGE was not stated by the cited sources and was removed.

key_value.quote: obtained a solar neutrino flux of 2.56 ± 0.16 (statistical error) ± 0.16 (systematic error) SNU
key_value.note: SNU is not one of the atlas's recognised dimensions; recorded with dimension `count`/unit "" as the closest representation, true unit given in `display`. The figure is the Cleveland et al. (1998) result as restated verbatim in the Davis Nobel lecture; the IOP abstract page carries the same figure (with an OCR typo '0.l6' in the statistical error).

key_value_text.quote: we counted a total of 2200 37Ar atoms and obtained a solar neutrino flux of 2.56 ± 0.16 (statistical error) ± 0.16 (systematic error) SNU
key_value_text.note: The IOP abstract page (src:homestake-1998-flux-measurement) calls it a 'solar neutrino-induced 37Ar production rate' (108 extractions) with the same figure; the exact statistical-error digits are quoted from the Davis Nobel lecture because the IOP page text has an OCR typo ('0.l6').

significance.note: A rate measurement, not a discovery/observation/evidence claim with a single sigma; no significance figure applies.
